residue.text: Preserved deferred INV proposal: compare enabled 900 rpm optical control, capped at second 105, with a fixed 60-second 900 rpm run logging shadow decisions. Hypothesis: severing feedback reduces stirring while both meet the sample target. Rival hypothesis: extra agitation improves final samples. Different cessation times create unequal quiet durations; no matched 900 rpm samples or observed feedback prolongation establish this loop. The retained six-arm-trial allocation leaves no additional slots.

Preserved deferred INV proposal: matched fixed-duration 300/900 rpm trials, optionally repeating in reverse order with a seconds-45-to-50 pause and stopping at second 65 to retain 60 stirring seconds. Hypothesis: stopping rapidly reduces agitation-generated optical disturbance; rivals include gradients or persistent artifacts. Pauses alter transport and settling. Specks and depression cannot establish bubbles or pre-stop uniformity; these comparisons would require reallocating trials.

Preserved stage1 limitations: directed transfers might improve vertical transport but also disturb gradients. Sampling can alter gradients. Reference repeatability is not concentration calibration; absolute concentration and bubble fraction remain unmeasurable. Two repeats cannot settle causal attribution.

Preserved stage1 and ATT uncertainty: one 300 rpm success does not establish reliable sufficiency; failures cannot justify a necessity claim for 900 rpm. Its total duration and matched samples are absent, preventing comparative time-saving or uniformity claims. Commanded speeds lack independent verification. Other recipes and scales remain untested; no real chemical or human benefit is established.

summary.text: Observed synthetic 300 rpm stirring stopped at second 60 and yielded final-vial attenuations 0.204, 0.209, 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounds the necessity claim for sustained 900 rpm and optical stability. ATT supports testing repeatability; INV supplies an unobserved disturbance-feedback hypothesis, not an explanation established by these observations.

Retain stage1 proposed alternatives, twice each: 300 rpm for 60 seconds; 600 rpm for 60 seconds; four 20 mL low-to-high syringe transfers completed at seconds 15, 30, 45, 60 without rotation. Order: 300, 600, syringe, syringe, 600, 300. All future successes remain hypotheses.

Use 150 mL water, 0.30 mL dye, fresh rinsed vessel, one dye bottle, locked camera, fixed addition location and spill tray. Stop on escaping liquid. End operations at second 60; sample depths 10, 28, 45 mm at second 120 within ten seconds, alternating order within each arm. Maximum six trials in 90 minutes.

Log five-second images without feedback restarts or rescue stirring, raw vials, spread, failures, cessation times, stirring seconds and transfer effort separately. Hypothesis: both 300 rpm repeats meet the 4 percent sample proxy; rival hypothesis: failures with successful stronger or directed redistribution indicate insufficient mixing. Order dependence or universal failure leaves interpretation unresolved. Stable images alone cannot establish success.
